title: Let send threads keep the delivery rules they read

blocks.text: The mail service checks every outgoing message against its delivery rules: which recipient domains are blocked, and the largest message each domain accepts. Dozens of send threads read the rules for every message, thousands of times a second, and must never wait for a lock. The admin API changes the rules when a domain starts bouncing or a partner asks for a smaller limit.

Support has two complaints. During a busy hour of rule changes, a send thread that had read the rules for a message saw them change while it was still checking that message. And after a block, one send thread went on sending to the blocked domain for half an hour.

Finish the three `TODO`s of `Store` in `src/main/java/practice/DeliveryRules.java`: `block`, `unblock` and `setMaxSizeKb`. Changes come from one admin thread at a time. When you're done, every change applies to the rules read after it, and rules a send thread has already read keep answering as they did when it read them, so a message is never checked against rules that change under it. You may change how `Store` holds the rules. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: blocking, unblocking and a new size limit each show in the rules read after the change
rules a send thread read before a change still answer as they did when it read them
the store holds the rules in a volatile field or an AtomicReference, so a send thread that takes no lock is guaranteed to see each change

origin.section: volatile Covers Reads of the Field, Not the Object It Points To

concepts: A published object is never changed again: a change builds a new object and assigns it to the volatile field, so readers that already hold the old one keep a version that doesn't change under them.
